title: Pinned split realizations of finite reduced based root data
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-scheme means a scheme with a specified morphism to $S$. An $S$-group scheme is an $S$-scheme with $S$-morphisms multiplication $G\times_S G\to G$, identity $S\to G$, and inverse $G\to G$ satisfying associativity, unit and inverse diagrams [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]. A homomorphism preserves these operations. A closed subgroup is a subgroup scheme whose inclusion is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]; normal means that its points form a normal subgroup after every algebra extension. It is reductive if it is smooth, affine and of finite presentation over $S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and its geometric fibres $G_\Omega=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, for homomorphisms $A\to\Omega$ to algebraically closed fields, are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Here unipotent for a smooth affine group over an algebraically closed field means that all its points are unipotent matrices in a faithful finite-dimensional representation, where a matrix $u$ is unipotent if $(u-I)^n=0$ for some $n\geq1$.

A finite reduced root datum consists of a finite-rank free abelian group $M$, its dual $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Z)$, finite subsets $\Phi\subset M\setminus\{0\}$ and $\Phi^\vee\subset M^\vee\setminus\{0\}$, and a bijection $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^\vee$ between them, with $\langle\alpha,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2$. For each root, the reflections $m\mapsto m-\langle m,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ and $y\mapsto y-\langle\alpha,y\rangle\alpha^\vee$ preserve the root and coroot sets and their correspondence. Also $\mathbf Q\alpha\cap\Phi=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. A base $\Delta\subset\Phi$ is linearly independent over $\mathbf Q$ and every root has an expression as an integer linear combination of $\Delta$ whose nonzero coefficients are all positive or all negative. Write $\Phi^+$ for the positive roots. A based root datum is this datum with $\Delta$ specified. A based-datum isomorphism from $(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee,\Delta)$ to $(M\prime,\Phi\prime,(M\prime)^\vee,(\Phi\prime)^\vee,\Delta\prime)$ is a lattice isomorphism $u:M\to M\prime$ with $u(\Phi)=\Phi\prime$, $u(\Delta)=\Delta\prime$ and $(u\alpha)^\vee=\alpha^\vee\circ u^{-1}$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$. Empty roots and the empty base are allowed; the roots need not span $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

A pinned split realization over $A$ of a based root datum $\mathcal R$ is a reductive $S$-group scheme $G$ with a closed subgroup $T$, an identification $T\simeq D_A(M)$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group], and the following data and conditions. Each geometric fibre of $T$ is a maximal torus in that of $G$, meaning a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\geq0$ and maximal under inclusion among such subgroups; $\mathbf G_m=D(\mathbf Z)$. The characters and cocharacters corresponding to $m\in M$ and $y\in M^\vee$ are the constant monomial maps of this split torus: on coordinate rings they send $t\mapsto e_m$ and $e_m\mapsto t^{\langle m,y\rangle}$, respectively, with $\langle m,y\rangle=y(m)$. The roots and coroots of every geometric fibre, under these identifications, are precisely the prescribed corresponding $\alpha$ and $\alpha^\vee$. Geometric roots are the nonzero characters occurring in the adjoint action on the tangent Lie algebra; the coroot is $t\mapsto v_\alpha(\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1}))$ from the rank-one $\operatorname{SL}_2$ homomorphism, equivalently the unique cocharacter giving the rank-one Weyl reflection, in [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]. For $H=G$ or $T$, put $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\ker(H(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to H(A))$, using the dual numbers [def-sc-dual-numbers] and reduction $\epsilon\mapsto0$. Explicitly, for the coordinate algebra $B_H$ and identity map $c_H:B_H\to A$, such a point is $b\mapsto c_H(b)+\epsilon d(b)$, where $d:B_H\to A$ is $A$-linear and $d(bb\prime)=c_H(b)d(b\prime)+c_H(b\prime)d(b)$. The $A$-module operations are pointwise addition and scalar multiplication of these $d$. Put $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. For a commutative $A$-algebra $R$ put $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)=\ker(G(R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to G(R))$, whose points are $b\mapsto c(b)+\epsilon d(b)$ with $c:B_G\to R$ the composite of $c_G$ with $A\to R$ and $d:B_G\to R$ an $A$-linear map satisfying the same identity, with pointwise $R$-module operations; for $v\in\mathfrak g$ let $v_R$ be its image under $A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\to R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A point $t\in T(R)$, viewed in $G(R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$ through $T\subseteq G$ and $R\to R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, acts on $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)$ by conjugation $\operatorname{Ad}(t)(w)=twt^{-1}$, and under $T\simeq D_A(M)$ it is an $A$-algebra map $A[M]\to R$; write $\chi_m(t)\in R^\times$ for the image of $e_m$. Define $\mathfrak g_m=\{v\in\mathfrak g:\operatorname{Ad}(t)(v_R)=\chi_m(t)\,v_R$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $R$ and every $t\in T(R)\}$. Weights mean characters of this full torus action on all $A$-algebra points, not differentials of characters. Require $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak g_\alpha$, where the direct sum is that of [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], with each $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ free of rank one. The pinning is a chosen generator $X_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ for each $\alpha\in\Delta$. A pinning-compatible isomorphism inducing a specified based-datum isomorphism is an $S$-group isomorphism restricting on the tori to $D_A(u^{-1}):D_A(M)\to D_A(M\prime)$ and whose differential sends $X_\alpha$ to $X\prime_{u(\alpha)}$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$. Here the differential is postcomposition of dual-number points by the group isomorphism. A split realization means the same data with the generators and base forgotten; a split reductive group means one admitting such data. These are definitions of data and conditions, with no existence assertion.
